questions.question:
A current carrying solenoid is placed vertically and a particle of mass \(m\) with charge \(Q\) is released from rest. The particle moves along the axis of solenoid. If \(g\) is acceleration due to gravity then the acceleration \((a)~\) of the charged particle will satisfy:
1. \(a=g~~\)
2. \(a>g~~\)
3. \(a=0~~\)
4. \(0<a<g~~\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\vec F = q(\vec {v}\times \vec {B} )\) Step:Find the acceleration of the charge particle. As the charged particle is released and moves along the axis of the solenoid, then the velocity \(v\) is along the axis and magnetic field\(B\) is also along the axis. The magnetic force acting on the particle is given by; \(\vec F = q(\vec {v}\times \vec {B} )\) \(\Rightarrow F = 0~~~~~~~~[\text{Since}~v ~\text{is parallel to}~ B~ [\vec v \times \vec B=0]]\) So, no magnetic force acts on the particle. Only the force acting on the charge particle is gravity i.e.,\(F = mg\) \(\Rightarrow ma = mg\) \(\Rightarrow a = g\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

A straight wire segment \(AB\) of length \(6~\text{cm}\) carries a steady current of \(5~\text{A}.\) A point \(P\) is located such that \(PA=PB=5~\text{cm},\) as shown in the figure. The magnetic permeability of free space is \(\mu_0=4\pi \times 10^{-7}~\text{N-A}^{-2}.\) The magnitude of the magnetic field at \(P\) due to the current-carrying wire is:

 1. \(1.5\times 10^{-5}~\text{T}\)
2. \(3.0\times 10^{-5}~\text{T}\)
3. \(2.0\times 10^{-5}~\text{T}\)
4. \(2.5\times 10^{-5}~\text{T}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(B=\frac{\mu_0 i}{4 \pi \mathrm{d}}\left(\sin \theta_1+\sin \theta_2\right)\) Step 1: Find the perpendicular distance from point \(P\). Using Pythagoras theorem, \(d^2+\left(\frac{6}{2}\right)^2=5^2 \\ \Rightarrow d^2+3^2=5^2 \\ \Rightarrow d^2=25-9=16 \\ \Rightarrow d=4 \text{ cm}\) Step 2: Find the magnetic field at \(P\). \(B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}(\sin\theta_1+\sin\theta_2) \\ B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}(2\sin\theta) \quad [\because \theta_1=\theta_2=\theta]\) From the triangle \(POB\),\(\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}\) So, \(B=\frac{(4\pi\times10^{-7})(5)}{4\pi(4\times10^{-2})} \left(2\times\frac{3}{5}\right) \\ \Rightarrow B=\frac{5\times10^{-7}}{4\times10^{-2}}\times\frac{6}{5} \\ \Rightarrow B=\frac{6}{4}\times10^{-5} =1.5\times10^{-5}\text{ T}\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.
